body.statement: Can the root-ordered sparse-core extendability handle be realized by a finite partial-support state and child map such that every live child has a globally minimal completion, children partition all completions, completed supports are never dominated by another core, and the extension test runs in \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) time?
body.justification: This is the genuine open step: completed-support dominators are ordered, but their obligations have not been shown stable under partial extension across competing cores.
body.gap: Steiner branching supplies extension for fully selectable edge witnesses, and bounded-treewidth transversal branching supplies extension for an explicit hypergraph; neither provides this projected, implicit, cross-core extension oracle.
body.consumer: A positive resolution supplies the missing correctness and worst-delay invariant for the obstruction compiler; a negative resolution identifies the parameter that must replace \(b\).

obligation.what_is_open: A polynomial-size canonical state and child partition with a \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) nonempty-completion test for globally minimal supports across competing sparse cores.
obligation.obstruction: The sparse-core theorem controls each local hedge template but not the unbounded directed ancestry support. Minimality within one core is not stable under extensions from another core, and a leaf-only domination filter can traverse exponentially many completed supports that are globally dominated.
obligation.attempted: The root-private dominator ordering and ordinary include/exclude self-reduction were examined. The former is certified only after a completion is known; the latter requires deciding whether forced included edges survive global minimization, which does not follow from a monotone failure oracle.
obligation.partial_result: The sparse-core reduction is complete: every obstruction is a globally minimal set \(K_c\cup J\), every such global minimum is an obstruction, \(|K_c|\le2b-2\), and \(|\mathfrak C|\le |V|2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\).  What remains is an extension oracle that preserves global minimality across all cores without traversing exponentially many dominated completions.
